transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (RW AE), Ravi Patel (RW SE), Sofia Navarro (CTO - Orchard), Ethan Brooks (Head of ML), Priya Singh (SRE), Liam O'Connor (VP Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Quick kickoff to align on stability priorities, cost expectations, and next steps for a pilot. Action items captured.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro from Redwood side — I'm Maya, account lead, and Ravi is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Hey all. I'll mostly cover perf and bench details.
[00:18] Sofia Navarro: Hi thanks, Sofia here. we've been moving fast with the Orchard chat assistant and wanted to lock down cost and reliability plans.
[00:25] Ethan Brooks: Ethan — we own the model infra. current stack is mostly a mix of k8s on GCP and some FaaS for lightweight routes.
[00:34] Priya Singh: Priya, SRE — I'm mostly concerned about burst traffic and auditability.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: Liam, product. main success metric is latency under 350ms for web queries and 99.9% uptime for critical routes.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Awesome. quick agenda: usage snapshot, tradeoffs (latency/cost), security ask, pilot/bench scope, next steps. sound good?
[00:54] Sofia Navarro: Yep, go ahead.
[00:56] Maya Chen: Ravi, can you start with what we saw in the pre-call data? (note: Orchard shared anonymized traffic csv)
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Sure. so looking at the sample, typical QPS is around 120 sustained outside peak, with bursts 600-800 qps for 2-3 minute windows. average token length is short — 30 to 70 tokens per request — but tail latencies matter a lot. we simulated a small continuous batch and saw single-model hosted path latency median ~ 220ms but p95 closer to 480ms in our quick run — that p95 is what drives product pain. (slight pause) also caching helps a lot for prefixy queries, but for new generative prompts it's less possible.
[02:00] Ethan Brooks: The p95 numbers track with our telemetry. our cost driver is frequent short requests; token cost is lower per request but volume spikes ramp spend. we tried naive batching in k8s but it increased cold-start latencies.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Right — that's where Redwood's autoscaling and dedicated pools come in. with Dedicated you get predictable throughput, reduced cold-starts. downside is commit/rightsizing.
[02:28] Priya Singh: can you remind us on data retention for hosted vs dedicated vs private? we have compliance constraints for EU PII.
[02:36] Ravi Patel: Hosted: we offer retention options and can do customer-scoped logging, but if you need full control and on-prem keys you should look at Private. Dedicated sits in customer's tenancy but managed capacity, we can integrate with KMS for key custody. note — some of our docs may say 'Redwood Privet' — sorry that was typo in an earlier deck i saw.
[02:57] Sofia Navarro: (laughs) ok noted. we will need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 1 year. also SSO via SAML, RBAC for teams.
[03:08] Maya Chen: We can do that. we'll share the SOC2 / ISO and the KMS integration doc after the call — security whitepaper link: https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper.pdf (auto note).
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: On pricing, high level — does Redwood bill per token for hosted and dedicated? and how does dedicated commit work with bursts?
[03:30] Maya Chen: Hosted: per-token and embed units. Dedicated: reserved capacity monthly with burst credits; we model your 95th percentile baseline and offer a burst bucket for spikes. we'll put a few scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[03:42] Ethan Brooks: Are there any hidden overheads like KV cache warming or session state transfers?
[03:47] Ravi Patel: Good Q. KV cache is kept on the serving layer; session handoffs can add a few ms but not token-level costs. caching tends to reduce cost because repeated prefixes avoid recompute. props: sometimes the transcripts show 'KV cache' as 'K vs cache' in older notes — ignore those typos.
[04:03] Maya Chen: For the pilot we suggested a two-week bench: 1) Redwood-hosted baseline, 2) Dedicated small pool with autoscale, 3) Private dev (optional) to validate KMS and audit logs. we'll capture latency and per-token $ across those.
[04:17] Sofia Navarro: timeline wise — we want to decide on December exec readout. pilot results by end of November would be ideal.
[04:24] Maya Chen: That aligns. Ravi, what's a realistic bench time to produce meaningful numbers?
[04:29] Ravi Patel: With the sample traffic you provided and a small harness we'll get initial numbers in 4-5 business days; full comparative bench with a few load shapes is about a week. so target to share results by 2025-11-24.
[04:42] Priya Singh: Any concerns about network egress costs if we move to Dedicated in us-west? we have mixed region users.
[04:49] Ravi Patel: Egress is generally a cloud factor; we can simulate and show estimates. Dedicated in us-west reduces cross-region egress for west users but you'll want to route by region for global app. Redwood smart routing can failover to a cheaper region but we'll surface egress impact.
[05:05] Ethan Brooks: On reliability, what's the basic SLA for Dedicated?
[05:09] Maya Chen: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated customers — specifics in the enterprise SOW. separate support tiers for on-call and 24/7.
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: For the product team, we want to understand rollback behavior when a model degrades. how do rollouts and automatic fallback work?
[05:27] Ravi Patel: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. for example if a quantized variant underperforms we can route to a higher fidelity variant. there's a config layer to pin versions per route.
[05:41] Sofia Navarro: That sounds useful. we had an incident where model A's hallucination rate spiked and we had no quick fallback, so traffic kept going to the bad variant.
[05:51] Maya Chen: We'll show the rollout controls in the demo follow-up.
[05:55] Ethan Brooks: Security again — audit logs need to be searchable and tied to session ids. is that doable?
[06:01] Ravi Patel: Yes, audit logs can be shipped to your logging cluster or retained in our console with export. we can wire it to BigQuery or Elasticsearch on your side.
[06:09] Priya Singh: KMS key rotation cadence is a requirement. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[06:14] Ravi Patel: We integrate with cloud KMS and HSM, yes. will capture that in the security doc.
[06:20] Maya Chen: quick pivot to costs — Ethan said token-lengths are short. that normally favors smaller models but more frequent calls. have you profiled embedding vs generation split?
[06:30] Ethan Brooks: Embeddings are used for retrieval about 20% of the time. embeddings are cheaper per op but we do dense vector ops after. generation is heavy.
[06:37] Ravi Patel: We can recommend quantization and batching parameters for that profile; Redwood Optimize would suggest batching thresholds and a quant profile with minimal quality loss.
[06:48] Sofia Navarro: Do you have any public perf numbers we can compare to Anthropic/Bedrock?
[06:52] Ravi Patel: We have a benchmark spreadsheet; note that direct vendor-to-vendor comparisons are tricky because tokenization and sequence lengths differ. we'll share our benchmark sheet — link will be in the follow-up. (small pause) sometimes public names are mis-typed in our auto notes as 'Bedrocky' — apologies.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot acceptance criteria: we want p95 < 400ms for web route and cost per 1M requests under $X (we'll define X after bench). Also 1 year audit log retention and KMS in customer tenancy.
[07:22] Maya Chen: good acceptance criteria — we'll incorporate them.
[07:26] Ethan Brooks: Who from your side will run the bench and get us the infra commands?
[07:30] Ravi Patel: I'll set up a harness and share the load generator scripts. I'll also include the config used for batching, KV cache settings, and model variant names.
[07:40] Sofia Navarro: About model variants — we may want to test a quantized 8-bit variant for cost and a float16 for quality.
[07:47] Ravi Patel: yep, we'll include both. also we'll instrument token breakdowns so you can see where cost came from.
[07:55] Maya Chen: quick note on procurement — any long lead procurement items we should know about?
[07:59] Priya Singh: SSO provisioning and vendor security review usually takes 2-3 weeks. contract review might take similar.
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: finance will want a committed spend option if the Dedicated price per unit is attractive.
[08:12] Maya Chen: we'll put together a dedicated pricing scenario and a hosted-to-dedicated migration path.
[08:18] Ethan Brooks: Ok. one last technical — we use a custom tokenizer for some vendors; will that be a problem?
[08:24] Ravi Patel: Not usually — we support custom tokenization pipelines at inference time, though it can affect perf and token counts. include a sample and we'll test.
[08:33] Sofia Navarro: Great. can you also include a simple cost model that shows the impact of batching thresholds vs p95?
[08:39] Ravi Patel: yes, that's part of the Optimize recommendations. I'll include a couple of graphs and a scenario table in the spreadsheet.
[08:47] Maya Chen: let's recap next steps quickly. Sofia, you will confirm SLOs and compliance owners. Priya to send infra diagram. Ravi to run bench and share link. Maya to share pricing + security docs. agree?
[08:59] Sofia Navarro: yes. we'll aim for the dates discussed.
[09:03] Liam O'Connor: can we schedule the pilot kickoff week of 2025-11-25 pending bench numbers?
[09:09] Maya Chen: I'll send a calendar invite with tentative times.
[09:12] Ethan Brooks: quick question — any known limitations for token streaming with function call style responses? we've had flaky streams in a previous vendor.
[09:21] Ravi Patel: Redwood streaming is generally stable; occasional drop-offs can happen if network blips. there's a streaming batch path and a single-token flush path depending on latency profile. we'll instrument that in the bench.
[09:33] Priya Singh: Are there diagnostics for tracing requests through the stack? we need distributed traces correlated to sessions.
[09:38] Ravi Patel: yes we emit traces and support trace contexts. we'll provide examples for OpenTelemetry.
[09:45] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up — thanks everyone. we will follow up with the security pack, pricing scenarios, and the bench spreadsheet.
[09:54] Sofia Navarro: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:56] Meeting end.
